entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12487"/><div sID="gen22951" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12487"/>2. Parallel to <reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">Zec 14:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.3.4">3, 4</reference>, where the "Mount of Olives" answers to the "Valley of Jehoshaphat" here. The latter is called "the valley of blessing" (Berachah) (<reference osisRef="2Chr.20.26">2Ch 20:26</reference>). It lies between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives and has the Kedron flowing through it. As Jehoshaphat overthrew the confederate foes of Judah, namely, Ammon, Moab, &c. (<reference osisRef="Ps.83.6-Ps.83.8">Psa 83:6-8</reference>), in this valley, so God was to overthrow the Tyrians, Zidonians, Philistines, Edom, and Egypt, with a similar utter overthrow (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.4">Joe 3:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.19">19</reference>). This has been long ago fulfilled; but the ultimate event shadowed forth herein is still future, when God shall specially interpose to destroy Jerusalem's last foes, of whom Tyre, Zidon, Edom, Egypt, and Philistia are the types. As "Jehoshaphat" means "the judgment of Jehovah," the valley of Jehoshaphat may be used as a general term for the theater of God's final judgments on Israel's foes, with an allusion to the judgment inflicted on them by Jehoshaphat. The definite mention of the Mount of Olives in <reference osisRef="Zech.14.4">Zec 14:4</reference>, and the fact that this was the scene of the ascension, makes it likely the same shall be the scene of Christ's coming again: compare "this same Jesus ... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen Him go into heaven" (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.11">Ac 1:11</reference>).<div eID="gen22951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22952" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all nations--</hi>namely, which have maltreated Judah.<div eID="gen22952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22953" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">plead with them--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.66.16">Is 66:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.22">Eze 38:22</reference>).<div eID="gen22953" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22954" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my heritage Israel--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Deut.32.9">De 32:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.10.16">Jr 10:16</reference>). Implying that the source of Judah's redemption is God's free love, wherewith He chose Israel as His peculiar heritage, and at the same time assuring them, when desponding because of trials, that He would plead their cause as His own, and as if He were injured in their person. <div eID="gen22954" type="x-p"/>

Grecians--</hi>literally, "Javanites," that is, the Ionians, a Greek colony on the coast of Asia Minor who were the first Greeks known to the Jews. The Greeks themselves, however, in their original descent came from Javan (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.2">Ge 10:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.4">4</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12493"/><div sID="gen22965" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12493"/><hi type="bold">8. sell them to ... Sabeans--</hi>The Persian Artaxerxes Mnemon and Darius Ochus, and chiefly the Greek Alexander, reduced the Phoenician and Philistine powers. Thirty thousand Tyrians after the capture of Tyre by the last conqueror, and multitudes of Philistines on the taking of Gaza, were sold as slaves. The Jews are here said to do that which the God of Judah does in vindication of their wrong, namely, sell the Phoenicians who sold them, to a people "far off," as was Greece, whither the Jews had been sold. The Sabeans at the most remote extremity of Arabia Felix are referred to (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.6.20">Jr 6:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.12.42">Mt 12:42</reference>). <div eID="gen22965" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12494"/><div sID="gen22966" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12494"/>9. The nations hostile to Israel are summoned by Jehovah to "come up" (this phrase is used because Jerusalem was on a hill) against Jerusalem, not that they may destroy it, but to be destroyed by the Lord (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.7-Ezek.38.23">Eze 38:7-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.2-Zech.9.14">Zec 12:2-9; 14</reference>:2, 3).<div eID="gen22966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22967" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Prepare war--</hi>literally, sanctify war: because the heathen always began war with religious ceremonies. The very phrase used of Babylon's preparations against Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Jer.6.4">Jr 6:4</reference>) is now used of the final foes of Jerusalem. As Babylon was then desired by God to advance against her for her destruction, so now all her foes, of whom Babylon was the type, are desired to advance against her for their own destruction. <div eID="gen22967" type="x-p"/>

Prepare war-- literally, sanctify war: because the heathen always began war with religious ceremonies. The very phrase used of Babylon's preparations against Jerusalem ( Jr 6:4 ) is now used of the final foes of Jerusalem. As Babylon was then desired by God to advance against her for her destruction, so now all her foes, of whom Babylon was the type, are desired to advance against her for their own destruction.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12495"/><div sID="gen22968" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12495"/><hi type="bold">10. Beat your ploughshares into swords--</hi>As the foes are desired to "beat their ploughshares into swords, and their pruning hooks into spears," that so they may perish in their unhallowed attack on Judah and Jerusalem, so these latter, and the nations converted to God by them, after the overthrow of the antichristian confederacy, shall, on the contrary, "beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning hooks," when under Messiah's coming reign there shall be war no more (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.4">Is 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.18">Ho 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.3">Mi 4:3</reference>).<div eID="gen22968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22969" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let the weak say, I am strong--</hi>So universal shall be the rage of Israel's foes for invading her, that even the weak among them will fancy themselves strong enough to join the invading forces. Age and infirmity were ordinarily made valid excuses for exemption from service, but so mad shall be the fury of the world against God's people, that even the feeble will not desire to be exempted (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.2.1-Ps.2.3">Psa 2:1-3</reference>). <div eID="gen22969" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12496"/><div sID="gen22970" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12496"/><hi type="bold">11. Assemble--</hi>"Hasten" [Maurer].<div eID="gen22970" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22971" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thither--</hi>to the valley of Jehoshaphat.<div eID="gen22971" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22972" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy mighty ones--</hi>the warriors who fancy themselves "mighty ones," but who are on that very spot to be overthrown by Jehovah [Maurer]. Compare "the mighty men" (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9">Joe 3:9</reference>). Rather, Joel speaks of God's really "mighty ones" in contrast to the self-styled "mighty men" (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9">Joe 3:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.103.20">Psa 103:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.13.3">Is 13:3</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Dan.10.13">Da 10:13</reference>). Auberlen remarks: One prophet supplements the other, for they all prophesied only "in part." What was obscure to one was revealed to the other; what is briefly described by one is more fully so by another. Daniel calls Antichrist a king, and dwells on his worldly conquests; John looks more to his spiritual tyranny, for which reason he adds a second beast, wearing the semblance of spirituality. Antichrist himself is described by Daniel. Isaiah (<reference osisRef="Isa.29.1-Isa.29.24">Is 29:1-24</reference>), Joel (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.21">Joe 3:1-21</reference>) and Zechariah (Zec 12:<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.21">1-14:21</reference>), describe his army of heathen followers coming up against Jerusalem, but not Antichrist himself. <div eID="gen22972" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 11. Assemble-- "Hasten" [Maurer]. thither-- to the valley of Jehoshaphat. thy mighty ones-- the warriors who fancy themselves "mighty ones," but who are on that very spot to be overthrown by Jehovah [Maurer]. Compare "the mighty men" ( Joe 3:9 ). Rather, Joel speaks of God's really "mighty ones" in contrast to the self-styled "mighty men" ( Joe 3:9 ; Psa 103:20 ; Is 13:3 ; compare Da 10:13 ). Auberlen remarks: One prophet supplements the other, for they all prophesied only "in part." What was obscure to one was revealed to the other; what is briefly described by one is more fully so by another. Daniel calls Antichrist a king, and dwells on his worldly conquests; John looks more to his spiritual tyranny, for which reason he adds a second beast, wearing the semblance of spirituality. Antichrist himself is described by Daniel. Isaiah ( Is 29:1-24 ), Joel ( Joe 3:1-21 ) and Zechariah (Zec 12: 1-14:21 ), describe his army of heathen followers coming up against Jerusalem, but not Antichrist himself.
entries.reader_content_plain: 11. Assemble-- "Hasten" [Maurer]. thither-- to the valley of Jehoshaphat. thy mighty ones-- the warriors who fancy themselves "mighty ones," but who are on that very spot to be overthrown by Jehovah [Maurer]. Compare "the mighty men" ( Joe 3:9 ). Rather, Joel speaks of God's really "mighty ones" in contrast to the self-styled "mighty men" ( Joe 3:9 ; Psa 103:20 ; Is 13:3 ; compare Da 10:13 ). Auberlen remarks: One prophet supplements the other, for they all prophesied only "in part." What was obscure to one was revealed to the other; what is briefly described by one is more fully so by another. Daniel calls Antichrist a king, and dwells on his worldly conquests; John looks more to his spiritual tyranny, for which reason he adds a second beast, wearing the semblance of spirituality. Antichrist himself is described by Daniel. Isaiah ( Is 29:1-24 ), Joel ( Joe 3:1-21 ) and Zechariah (Zec 12: 1-14:21 ), describe his army of heathen followers coming up against Jerusalem, but not Antichrist himself.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12498"/><div sID="gen22975" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12498"/>13. God does not cut off the wicked at once, but waits till their guilt is at its full (so as to the Amorites' iniquity, <reference osisRef="Gen.15.16">Ge 15:16</reference>), to show forth His own long-suffering, and the justice of their doom who have so long abused it (Mt 13:27-30, 38, 40; <reference osisRef="Rev.14.15-Rev.14.19">Re 14:15-19</reference>). Lord ... water ... valley of Shittim--</hi>The blessings, temporal and spiritual, issuing from Jehovah's house at Jerusalem, shall extend even to Shittim, on the border between Moab and Israel, beyond Jordan (<reference osisRef="Num.25.1">Nu 25:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Num.33.49">33:49</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.2.1">Jos 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.6.5">Mi 6:5</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12504"/><div sID="gen22989" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12504"/><hi type="bold">19. Edom--</hi>It was subjugated by David, but revolted under Jehoram (<reference osisRef="2Chr.21.8-2Chr.21.10">2Ch 21:8-10</reference>); and at every subsequent opportunity tried to injure Judah. Egypt under Shishak spoiled Jerusalem under Rehoboam of the treasures of the temple and the king's house; subsequently to the captivity, it inflicted under the Ptolemies various injuries on Judea. Antiochus spoiled Egypt (<reference osisRef="Dan.11.40-Dan.11.43">Da 11:40-43</reference>). Edom was made "desolate" under the Maccabees [Josephus, Antiquities, 12.11,12]. The low condition of the two countries for centuries proves the truth of the prediction (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.19.1">Is 19:1</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Jer.49.17">Jr 49:17</reference>; Ob 10). So shall fare all the foes of Israel, typified by these two (<reference osisRef="Isa.63.1">Is 63:1</reference>, &c.). <div eID="gen22989" type="x-p"/>
